subject: Audit chronicle snapshot & handback — admin activity logs for SIG/SOC2
messages:
From: Todd Liang <todd.liang@bluewaterhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: security@bluewaterhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit snapshot request — admin actions / operator activity

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG and SOC 2 intake for BlueWater Health, we need an extract of admin/operator activity for a scoped period (2029-04-01 to 2029-04-30). Specifically:

- All privileged/admin API calls (create/delete/role-change) with caller identity, resource, request_id and full timestamps.
- Session start/stop, sudo/elevation events, console/SSH access markers and source IP.
- Any configuration changes to model pinning / routing / rollout policies.
- Retain sequence so we can reconstruct causality (order matters).

Two asks:
1) What fields are included in your admin event schema (we prefer a precise list, e.g., user_id, user_email_hash, action, resource_type, resource_id, timestamp_utc, region, ip_address, request_id, payload_hash)?
2) What delivery/export options do you support for a verified evidence handback (signed manifest, HMAC per-file, md5/sha256 checksums, delivery to our S3 or an SFTP endpoint)?

We also need the retention baseline you apply to raw events versus aggregated/analytics copies. If there are PII considerations (e.g., request payloads containing customer data), describe redaction or hashing approaches.

Can you send a proposed delivery plan and ETA? BlueWater Security team will need the manifest and verification steps documented.

Cheers,
Todd
T. Liang
Security Operations — BlueWater Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Todd Liang <todd.liang@bluewaterhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit snapshot request — admin actions / operator activity

Todd — thanks for the clear scope. Outline below is what we can provide and an export plan. Looping Kim and Marissa for delivery and custody.

1) Event schema (admin_event.ndjson):
- timestamp_utc
- sequence_id (monotonic per-tenant)
- event_type (e.g., ADMIN_CREATE, ADMIN_DELETE, ROLE_ASSIGN, ROUTE_CHANGE, ELEVATION_START, ELEVATION_END)
- actor_id (internal user id)
- actor_email (hashed: sha256(email) by default; can provide unhashed if contractual)
- actor_role
- target_resource_type
- target_resource_id
- request_id (trace id)
- client_ip
- region
- user_agent
- api_endpoint
- change_summary (short text / JSON diff truncated)
- full_payload_ref (pointer to payload in evidence bucket; may be redacted)
- audit_level (raw|redacted|aggregated)

2) Retention model:
- Raw admin events: default 90 days (retained in compressed ndjson).
- Secured snapshot archives: on-request we can produce and retain an attested snapshot for up to 2 years under a controlled handback agreement.
- Aggregated metrics (counts by action/actor): retained 2 years by default; older aggregated indices are 24 months.
- Note on PII: request payloads that include customer content are redacted by default in the public evidence extracts; we replace with payload hashes and provide redacted/unredacted toggles under NDA with documented chain-of-custody.

3) Export options & verification:
- Formats: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) compressed as tar.gz or gzip; parquet export available for large analytical loads.
- Delivery: secure S3 direct-write to your bucket (cross-account role), SFTP push (customer-managed endpoint), or pre-signed multi-part download link with 7-day TTL.
- Integrity: per-file sha256 checksums in a signed manifest CSV. Optionally HMAC-SHA256 over the manifest using a customer-shared key.
- Chain of custody: signed manifest with 2048-bit RSA signature (we provide public key), and an optional notarized timestamp (on-request).
- Streaming alternative: Kafka mirror (if you prefer near-real-time replay for a narrow window).

4) Sampling & scope tuning:
- Full export (every raw admin event) — default for evidence requests.
- Timebox + sampling: for long periods we can produce a full manifest of events and a sampled subset with sampling ration documented.
- Redaction policy: we can provide two bundles — 1) redacted bundle safe for public archive; 2) unredacted bundle under an evidence access agreement.

Delivery ETA:
- Draft manifest + sample ndjson (first 48 hours).
- Full export tar.gz (up to 72 hours for a 30-day window; longer if retention-tiering required).

Action items: 
- Todd: confirm destination (S3 cross-account role ARN or SFTP host), and whether you need unhashed emails.
- BlueWater: confirm whether you require HMAC over manifest.

Thanks — I’ll start the snapshot job once we get the target endpoint.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference

From: security@bluewaterhealth.com <security@bluewaterhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: todd.liang@bluewaterhealth.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 13:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit snapshot request — admin actions / operator activity

Aditya,

Thanks for the detailed breakdown. A few clarifications before we finalize: 

- We will supply an S3 bucket and cross-account role ARNs. Please prepare both a redacted and unredacted bundle. For the unredacted bundle we will require: unhashed actor_email, full_payload_ref content (only for entries where payload contains non-PHI customer identifiers), and the signed manifest with HMAC.
- For request ordering: we need sequence_id monotonic across the timebox and a guaranteed UTC timestamp with millisecond precision. Can you confirm you include timezone-normalized timestamps and sequence_id gaps are provably reconstruction-safe?
- For privileged sessions, do you include both session start/end and elevated-exec records (e.g., commands run during elevation)? If command-level logs are not available, please state limitations.
- For region and IP privacy, we need source IP and geolocation at export time. If you obfuscate IPs in the redacted bundle, document the algorithm.

Also please include the small sample manifest and an example of the signed manifest verification command we can run locally (openssl or aws-cli examples).

Regards,
BlueWater Security

BlueWater team — finalizing plan and confirming deliverables. Answers inline and next steps below.

- Timestamps & sequencing: we will export timestamp_utc with ISO8601 millisecond precision (e.g. 2029-04-02T14:03:12.123Z). sequence_id is assigned per-tenant and monotonic; we will include a manifest field "sequence_ranges" so you can detect gaps and verify continuity.

- Privileged session capture: we record session_start/session_end and export elevated_exec metadata (command summary + exec duration). We do not store full terminal transcript by default except when session recording is enabled on the org; if you require transcripts those can be included under the unredacted bundle (note: transcripts may contain customer PII).

- IP & geo: raw_ip exported in unredacted bundle; redacted bundle will substitute ip_hash (sha256(ip||salt)) and a coarse geo field (country only). Documented algorithm and salt handling will be in the signed manifest.

- Verification instructions (example):
1) Download bundle and manifest from s3://your-bucket/bluewater/2029-05-14/
2) Verify file checksums: sha256sum -c manifest-sha256.csv
3) Verify manifest signature: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public_key.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.csv
4) Optional HMAC verification (if HMAC agreed): echo -n "$(cat manifest.csv)" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "<shared-key>"

Delivery plan: 
- Today: sample manifest + one-day ndjson sample (attached) and example verification commands.
- Thu 2029-05-16 02:00 UTC: full export to your S3 (cross-account role). You will receive an email with s3 path, manifest.csv, manifest.sig, and manifest-hmac.txt (if agreed).
- Retention on our side: we will mark the snapshot as "evidence-handback" and retain an identical copy for 24 months for dispute resolution.

Attachments included with this message: sample-ndjson-admin-events-20290430.tar.gz (contains 72 hours of redacted and unredacted sample files), example-manifest.csv

Next steps: Todd, confirm cross-account role ARN and whether you want HMAC. Kim/Marissa — please open a custody ticket and prepare RSA keypair for manifest signing.

Regards,
Aditya
Head of Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference
